correctness.rationale: The Stirling-permutation insertion representation has 2t-1 equiprobable gaps at birth t. If earlier labels S remain adjacent, precisely |S intersect [1,t-1]| gaps are forbidden; once split an adjacent equal pair cannot reform. Multiplication proves every finite-subset joint survival identity. For i<j, the ratio of two survival probabilities is product_{k=j}^{n-1}(1-1/(4k^2)), giving strictly negative pair covariance for j<n. Log-product asymptotics yield n Cov(I_i,I_j)->-(1-y)sqrt(x/y)/4 for 0<x<y<1. Bounds p_{n,i}<=sqrt(i/n) and n|Cov|<=1/2 control the origin; diagonal and off-diagonal Riemann sums integrate to K(s,t)=s^{3/2}(6-3sqrt(t)+t^{3/2})/9-s²/3 for s<=t. Independently enumerated all insertion words for n<=6 and all subset survival probabilities exactly; the infinite kernel is analytic, not inferred from finite enumerations.
